entries.topic: From campaign to office: endorsement, the efficiency commission idea, the DOGE announcement and op-ed, Ramaswamy's exit

claims.text: Musk posted on X on the evening of 13 July 2024, after the Butler shooting: 'I fully endorse President Trump and hope for his rapid recovery'

5 Sept 2024 Economic Club of New York: Trump said he would create a government efficiency commission 'tasked with conducting a complete financial and performance audit of the entire federal government' and 'making recommendations for drastic reforms'; first time he said Musk had agreed to lead it; plan to eliminate 'fraud and improper payments' within six months; Musk had said on an 19 August podcast he would be interested; Musk on X 5 Sept: 'I look forward to serving America if the opportunity arises'

Trump's statement (12 Nov 2024, reported 13 Nov): Musk and Ramaswamy 'will pave the way for my Administration to dismantle Government Bureaucracy, slash excess regulations, cut wasteful expenditures, and restructure Federal Agencies'; could be 'The Manhattan Project' of our time; they would provide advice and guidance from outside of Government; deadline 4 July 2026; Musk: 'This will send shockwaves through the system, and anyone involved in Government waste, which is a lot of people!'

Musk–Ramaswamy WSJ op-ed, 20 Nov 2024: 'We will serve as outside volunteers, not federal officials or employees'; 'Instead of new laws, existing legislation will lead DOGE to make the changes'; president 'can, by executive action, immediately pause the enforcement of those regulations'; cites Loper Bright (2024) and West Virginia v. EPA; DOGE would 'identify the minimum number of employees required at an agency'; '$500 billion plus in annual federal expenditures that are unauthorized by Congress'

Op-ed pledged to identify 'thousands' of regulations by 'unelected bureaucrats' for elimination and 'a significant reduction in the federal workforce'; Constitution as 'North Star for reform' (Jurist wording)

20 Jan 2025: Ramaswamy's departure confirmed hours after inauguration; spokeswoman Anna Kelly: he 'played a critical role in helping us create DOGE', 'intends to run for elected office soon', and 'the structure that we announced today' requires him to remain outside DOGE

entries.topic: DOGE's legal form: EO 14158, 5 USC 3161, SGEs, the administrator question, FACA and FOIA, GAO personnel report, the end of the temporary organization

claims.text: EO 14158 §3: U.S. Digital Service 'publicly renamed as the United States DOGE Service (USDS)', 'established in the Executive Office of the President'; a USDS Administrator in the EOP 'who shall report to the White House Chief of Staff'; a U.S. DOGE Service Temporary Organization under 5 U.S.C. 3161 'dedicated to advancing the President's 18-month DOGE agenda' that 'shall terminate on July 4, 2026'; agency heads to set up a DOGE Team 'of at least four employees', typically 'one DOGE Team Lead, one engineer, one human resources specialist, and one attorney', may include SGEs, within thirty days

EO 14158 §4: Software Modernization Initiative; agency heads 'to ensure USDS has full and prompt access to all unclassified agency records, software systems, and IT systems'; 'USDS shall adhere to rigorous data protection standards' (undefined); §2 agency definition excludes the EOP; §5 'subject to the availability of appropriations'; no enforceable rights

5 U.S.C. 3161(a): a temporary organization is one 'established by law or Executive order for a specific period not in excess of three years' and 'terminated upon the completion of the study or project'; (b) head may appoint staff outside chapter 51 rules; appointments may not exceed three years, extendable up to two more

The EO made DOGE an official but temporary part of the EOP instead of the outside task force announced in November; USDS launched under Obama after the troubled HealthCare.gov rollout; a FACA suit (AFGE, Public Citizen, State Democracy Defenders Fund) argued DOGE lacked 'a fair balance of viewpoints', closed meetings, non-public records

3 Feb 2025: White House official said Musk is a 'special government employee', unpaid, with a government email and White House office space; unlikely to need to file a public financial disclosure; SGEs usually appointed for up to 130 days; Trump: 'I think Elon is doing a good job. He's a big cost-cutter'

25 Feb 2025: earlier that day Leavitt declined to name DOGE's leader ('There are career officials and there are political appointees who are helping run DOGE on a day-to-day basis'); the previous day a government lawyer told a judge he did not know who the administrator was; that afternoon the White House named Amy Gleason acting administrator; she worked at USDS 2018–2021 on the federal COVID response and returned in January 2025; previously chief product officer at Russell Street Ventures and Main Street Health; White House said Musk oversees the effort as senior adviser, not a DOGE employee

Gleason declaration in CREW v. USDS (filed c. 14 March 2025): 'Elon Musk does not work at USDS'; 'I do not report to him, and he does not report to me'; 'To my knowledge, he is a Senior Advisor to the White House'; she reports to Chief of Staff Susie Wiles

4 Mar 2025 joint address: Trump: 'I have created the brand new Department of Government Efficiency, DOGE', 'which is headed by Elon Musk, who is in the gallery tonight'; plaintiffs in the FACA suit cited it the next day

18 Mar 2025: Judge Chuang found Musk likely violated the Appointments Clause; denying the claim because Musk lacks formal authority 'would open the door to an end-run around the Appointments Clause'; Musk may be 'exercising significant authority on governmental matters'; preliminary injunction on USAID shutdown steps

28 Mar 2025: Fourth Circuit (Quattlebaum, Niemeyer; Gregory concurring in result) stayed Chuang's order; Quattlebaum: 'unconventional does not necessarily equal unconstitutional'; evidence shows 'a strong likelihood that he functioned as an advisor to the President'; Gregory concurred only because the wrong defendants were sued

20 Jan 2025: four suits filed within minutes of the inauguration — three under FACA (APHA/VoteVets/CREW; National Security Counselors; Public Citizen) in D.D.C., and a FOIA suit by Center for Biological Diversity v. OMB
New York Sun, 22 Jan 2025: rebranding an existing White House office as DOGE 'may nullify' the advisory-committee challenges

Public Citizen v. Trump (D.D.C., 25-cv-164, Judge Cobb): consolidated with APHA v. OMB and Lentini v. DOGE; Public Citizen plaintiffs dismissed 3 Mar 2025 and APHA 12 May 2025 (both without prejudice); defendants' 11 Apr 2025 motion to dismiss (no private right of action under FACA; Article II) pending; defendants argued Musk as presidential adviser falls within FACA's all-employee exclusion; docket active into June 2026, no relief granted

10 Mar 2025: Judge Christopher Cooper (D.D.C.) found DOGE likely subject to FOIA, citing its 'unusual secrecy' and 'substantial authority over vast swathes of the federal government'; ordered expedited processing of three CREW requests and preservation

6 June 2025 Supreme Court order: stay granted, application treated as cert petition and granted; D.C. Circuit mandamus denial vacated and remanded; parts of the April 15 discovery order requiring disclosure of the content of USDS recommendations 'are not appropriately tailored'; 'separation of powers concerns counsel judicial deference and restraint'; did not decide whether USDS is a FOIA agency — that inquiry 'cannot turn on the entity's ability to persuade'; Sotomayor, Kagan, Jackson would have denied

15 Oct 2026: Supreme Court granted cert in U.S. DOGE Service v. U.S. District Court for D.C., No. 25-1103 — whether CREW may get discovery to show USDS is subject to FOIA; core issue whether USDS 'wields independent authority or is merely a board that exists to advise the president'; argument early 2027; D.C. Circuit had approved CREW's narrowed requests

GAO-26-108403 (5 Aug 2026): 206 DOGE personnel held EOP positions 20 Jan 2025–31 Jan 2026 (4 described as leaders); 27 were SGEs; at least 128 had separated; EOP did not provide training records or financial disclosures; nine agencies reported on 64 personnel (49 ethics training, 18 records training, 38 financial disclosures); ten agencies did not provide information; temporary organization terminated 4 July 2026; OGE has not reviewed an EOP ethics program since 2023 and has no plans to review USDS's

Nextgov 6 Aug 2026: the 27 SGEs include Musk; 127 of 206 were USDS employees with expert/consultant titles; GAO: 'Since the EO does not call for the termination of the broader USDS entity', USDS and agency staff could keep advancing DOGE initiatives; White House did not respond

Reuters 23 Nov 2025: OPM Director Scott Kupor said DOGE 'doesn't exist' and is no longer a 'centralized entity'; no workforce-reduction target; OPM took over many functions; Gebbia heads National Design Studio (August EO); Gleason became an adviser to HHS Secretary Kennedy in March per a court filing; Terrell HHS CTO; Rachel Riley Office of Naval Research; Jeremy Lewin oversees foreign assistance at State; hiring freeze over; White House spokeswoman Liz Huston: Trump 'continues to actively deliver on that commitment'

E&E 2 Jul 2026: temporary organization terminates 4 July 2026; USDS appears to remain; April FY2027 budget sought $35 million for USDS; House appropriators directed 'the Administrator of DOGE' to submit quarterly reports on hires, detailees and transfers; Gleason listed as acting administrator and reported to lead a CMS health-technology office; Terrell and Coristine moved to National Design Studio; Kupor later said DOGE principles 'remain alive and well'; Musk in December 2025 on the Katie Miller Podcast called DOGE 'a little bit successful' and said he would not do it again; savings page not updated since 1 January
